notes: PARENT-TOO-OLD flag RESOLVED as a documented fact, not a data error (research 2026-07-04): Sarah Wells is not a bare tree stub but a well-known Orange County, NY regional-history figure -- reputedly the first female European settler of the Wawayanda Patent (Goshen area), subject of a dedicated 1974 book-length genealogy (Emma McWhorter, Dolly Booth & Philip Seaman, 'The History and Genealogy of the William Bull and Sarah Wells Family of Orange County, New York'), the preserved Bull Stone House (Hamptonburgh, NY; maintained by the Bull Stone House Association), and repeated Chronicle-Network local-history features. Multiple independent secondary sources state she bore 12 children (5 sons, 7 daughters) with William Bull, 'the last being born just before Sarah's 52nd birthday' -- i.e. Elenor/Eleanor (Bull) Weller's 4 Mar 1745 birth at maternal age ~50-51 is the family's own well-attested capstone fact, not a misattached grandchild. All 12 children are reported to have lived to adulthood, married, and raised families.

Her own extreme lifespan (100-102 years) is independently corroborated by Find A Grave memorial 19421740, WikiTree Wells-121, Geni, and local press, all agreeing she died 21 Apr 1796 -- but the underlying birth year has genuine ambiguity IN THE SOURCE TRADITION ITSELF, not a tree error: per the Bull Stone House Association, descendants' family bibles disagree between 6 Apr 1694 (yielding the widely repeated '102 years, 15 days') and 6 Apr 1696 (yielding 100 years, 15 days) -- no birth record exists; colonial New York predates civil registration. The tree's current 1694 date matches the majority of secondary sources (Find A Grave, WikiTree, Geni, Chronicle) and is left as-is; flagged as an open question rather than corrected, since no primary source resolves it.

NEW FINDING: the 1974 family genealogy names 12 children total; this tree currently carries only 10. The two missing are Esther (Bull) Miller (b. 31 May 1731, m. John Miller of Montgomery, NY, 8 children) and Richard Bull -- neither has a record id in this dataset, so none was fabricated; flagged as an open question/backlog item for future addition rather than invented.

NEW FINDING: as a widow (William Bull d. 1755), Sarah reportedly remarried Johannes (John) Miller, a German Lutheran settler of Montgomery, NY, sometime between 1756 and 1770; she separated from him ('essentially divorced') in 1770 and returned to the Bull Stone House for the rest of her life. Not added as a formal second spouse relationship here because no record id exists for Johannes Miller in this dataset. Notably, her daughter Esther (Bull) Miller's husband John Miller appears to be this second husband's son -- i.e. a mother-and-daughter double-marriage into the same Miller family -- worth independent verification.

Direct-line note: the pedigree-continuing child in this tree is Margaret Bull (I182567600211, m. Silas Horton; daughter Sarah Horton I182534044137), not the flagged Elenor Weller (I182625971797), who is a genuine but collateral (non-direct-line) documented daughter.
